svg.desc: Figure S22. How SHMtrace turns reads into calls: six stages, each with its rule and equation, and the stage working on the JH4 libraries.

tspan.tspan: How SHMtrace decides what is a call
Every rule the engine applies, and the same rule working on the J
Every read is gated before it is used. A read over the length set for its locus,
or one whose quality scores predict more than one error in a hundred bases, is dropped.
Each read is aligned to the target, its paralogue and any contaminant at once,
and goes to whichever it matches best. A paralogue can also be analysed as a
The error rate is not taken from the quality scores. It is measured in the AID-null
libraries per substitution, strand and quality, pooled over positions as a floor; a
position whose controls err more keeps its own rate, shrunk toward the pooled one,
and every rate is inflated by one factor fitted by leaving each control out in turn.
Supporting reads are ranked by quality and every depth of evidence is tested
against that measured rate; the best test is kept and corrected for having tried
them all. A change carried by half the reads or more is set aside as likely germline.
Threshold set by the controls themselves
Each control is called against the other controls, giving decoy p-values. The
threshold is the largest at which the false calls the decoys predict are at most
Calls are summarised per library and compared between groups on the log scale,
with one value per animal, so clones of one lineage cannot stand in for
Each read goes to its best match
